openwrt_wiki.einleitung: The EAP 225 series are dual-band devices for different environments. The Outdoor and Wall models can only be powered by 802.3af/at PoE (48 V DC). The other models can also be powered via a 12V DC power supply.
installation_eap225_v3plus_outdoor: The EAP225-Outdoor, EAP225-Wall v2, EAP225 v3, and later models can be installed via the web interface after disabling Firmware Signature Check.
Upgrade the firmware to version v5.0.3, which fixes a bug that may cause the EAP to reboot abnormally during firmware upgrading and cause the device to brick
Enable the SSH-Server via the web interface (fallback IPv4 192.168.0.254); ssh into the target device and run 'cliclientd stopcs' to disable Firmware Signature Check
upload the factory image via the web interface, rename the firmware to something with less than 63 characters length
After the successfull update, the device can be reached at the default ip address 192.168.1.1
openwrt_wiki.warnung_2026_06: CRITICAL BRICK RISK (v5.1.1) - June 2026: Flashing directly from stock firmware v5.1.1 will brick the device. You must upgrade to v5.1.11 before installing OpenWrt. Tested only on EAP225 v3.0 Outdoor.
openwrt_wiki.warnung_2026_07: newer EAP225-Outdoor v3 APs are v3.20 hardware revision shipped with a 5.2.4 firmware which has a limited CLI. 'cliclientd stopcs' is not recognized anymore. At the moment, it's impossible to install OpenWRT at all, neither downgrade to 5.1.11 TP-Link firmware.
openwrt_wiki.hinweis_v320_aussehen: These new APs come in a new package that is bright green with dull green. The AP itself has Omada written on it instead of tp-link.
openwrt_wiki.hinweis_2026_09: Workaround für EAP615-Wall beschrieben, auf EAP225 ungetestet (Inhalt bewusst nicht übernommen: Umgehung einer Hersteller-Schutzfunktion)
openwrt_wiki.failsafe: Repower the router, the LED will stay bright a few seconds, then it will start flashing slowly: press the button repeatedly until the LED is flashing fast (beschrieben für EAP225-Wall, 'should work for all the EAP225 Serie devices')
openwrt_wiki.zurueck_zur_stock_firmware: aus Backup (mtdblock3 kernel + mtdblock4 rootfs zusammengefügt als sysupgrade) oder per tplink-safeloader -z aus TP-Link-Firmware

openwrt_git_v3.titel: ath79: support for TP-Link EAP225-Outdoor v3
openwrt_git_v3.autor: Paul Maruhn (Co-developed-by Philipp Rothmann; Tested-by Tido Klaassen; Signed-off-by Nick Hainke)
openwrt_git_v3.text: This model is almost identical to the EAP225-Outdoor v1. Major difference is the RTL8211FS PHY Chipset.
openwrt_git_v3.Flashing instructions: ssh into target device with recent (>= v1.6.0) firmware; run `cliclientd stopcs`; upload factory image via web interface
openwrt_git_v3.Debricking: To recover the device, you need access to the serial port. This requires fine soldering to test points, or the use of probe pins. Open the case and solder wires to the test points: RXD, TXD and TPGND4. Use a 3.3V UART, 115200 baud, 8n1. Interrupt bootloader by holding ctrl+B during boot; upload initramfs via built-in tftp client (tftp 0x80800000 initramfs.bin; bootelf $fileaddr), then sysupgrade
openwrt_git_v3.MAC addresses: MAC address (as on device label) is stored in device info partition at an offset of 8 bytes. ath9k device has same address as ethernet, ath10k uses address incremented by 1.

openwrt_git_v1.text: TP-Link EAP225-Outdoor v1 is an AC1200 (802.11ac Wave-2) pole or wall mount access point. Debricking requires access to the serial port, which is non-trivial.
openwrt_git_v1.UART: UART access tested by forum user arinc9.

openwrt_git_phy.text: This phy reset is required to have a working ethernet on the TP-Link EAP225-Outdoor v3 and EAP225 v4 after a reboot. Otherwise the ethernet port will only function properly on cold boots.

openwrt_git_mac.text: Commit e816591e226a ("ath79: qca: convert to nvmem-layout") mistakenly switched the source of the mac address from the 'info' to 'art' partition. ... tested to fix the problem for eap225-outdoor-v3
